Advantage Design Group is hiring an early-career Software Developer I to write, test, and maintain C# and .NET code for its Advantage Orientation and HR Engage platform. The role includes building platform features, troubleshooting issues, participating in code reviews and system design discussions, and collaborating with cross-functional teammates while developing technical skills.
Information Technology
SaaS
Software
Responsibilities
Write, test and maintain production code in C# and .NET, with guidance and code review from senior engineers
Build and update features across SQL Server, front-end pages and ADG’s content platform
Take part in code reviews, learning from feedback on your own work and offering thoughtful feedback to teammates
Join system design discussions and learn the reasoning behind the team’s architecture decisions
Troubleshoot and fix issues, and document what you learn so the whole team benefits
Work with designers, video producers, and project managers to bring client experiences to life
Participate in internal training, team projects, and peer mentorship to grow your skills
Qualification
C#
Object-Oriented Programming
.NET
ASP.NET MVC
ASP.NET Core
HTML
CSS
JavaScript
SQL
Git
RESTful APIs
Microsoft Azure
Required
Up to two years of professional software development experience. Internships, co-ops, coursework, and substantial personal projects count
Working knowledge of C# and object-oriented programming
Basic understanding of .NET and ASP.NET (MVC or Core)
Familiarity with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and SQL
Experience using Git or another version control system
Strong problem-solving and communication skills
In lieu of a degree, candidates with equivalent experience gained through prior work, internships, a coding program or substantial project work, demonstrating a working knowledge of C# and .NET development, will be considered
Ask questions early, take feedback well, and put it to work in the next thing you build
Own your tasks and keep them moving without frequent check-ins and speak up when you're stuck
Explain what you built and why in plain language, to engineers and to colleagues outside engineering
Test your own work, pay attention to detail, and keep the people using the platform in mind
Preferred
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Information Systems, or a related technical field preferred
Internship, co-op or professional experience on a .NET development team
Exposure to RESTful APIs, Razor, or a content management system such as Umbraco
Familiarity with Microsoft Azure, Azure DevOps or CI/CD pipelines
Awareness of web accessibility (WCAG) and secure coding practices
A portfolio, GitHub profile or project you can walk us through
Benefits

Profit sharing
Health, dental and vision coverage
Paid vacation
Flex time
Gym membership
Company-funded training
Mentorship from senior engineers
A defined career path with clear expectations at each step
Once established in the role, a hybrid schedule with two remote days per week
